question_text: If x² + y² − 4x + 6y + c = 0 represents a circle with radius 6, find the value of c.

mark_split.label: Read g, f, c and the radius formula

insider_note: This is the same question as its twin with 4 replaced by 6, so a student who has done one should reach the answer in two lines — the bigger radius simply forces a more negative constant.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Read g, f, c and the radius formula
steps.margin_note: One mark. The letters are different but the circle is the same one as in the twin question.
steps.memory_tip: Radius = √(g² + f² − c). Only the constant is unknown.
steps.why: The x and y coefficients are the same as in the previous question, so g² + f² = 13 again. Only the value the radius is set to has changed.
common_mistakes: Using the given radius 6 as g or f.

steps.label: Square and solve for c
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 6² = 36, so the constant has to be well below zero.
steps.why: A larger radius needs a larger value of g² + f² − c, and since g² + f² is fixed at 13, c has to fall. That is why the answer is well below zero.
